promptEs: En Do mayor, el acorde Re♭ mayor (Re♭, Fa, La♭) aparece como subdominante de color. ¿Qué número romano le corresponde?
promptEn: In C major, the D♭ major chord (D♭, F, A♭) appears as a dark-coloured subdominant. Which Roman numeral does it get?
explanationEs: En Do mayor, el segundo grado es Re. La napolitana baja ese grado un semitono a Re♭ y construye una tríada mayor: Re♭-Fa-La♭. Se cifra ♭II porque la fundamental está rebajada y la cualidad es mayor. No es el ii diatónico (Re-Fa-La), que es menor.
explanationEn: In C major the second degree is D. The Neapolitan lowers it by a semitone to D♭ and builds a major triad: D♭-F-A♭. It is labelled ♭II because the root is lowered and the quality is major. It is not the diatonic ii (D-F-A), which is minor.
